A quadratic equation is given by $$ x^2 - (k+2)x + (k+5) = 0, $$ where \(k\) is a real constant. (a) Find the discriminant of the equation in terms of \(k\). **[4 marks]** (b) Determine the values of \(k\) for which the equation has equal roots. **[4 marks]** (c) Find the range of values of \(k\) for which the equation has two distinct real roots. **[4 marks]** (d) Solve the inequality $$ x^2 - 5x + 6 < 0 $$ and illustrate the solution on a number line. **[4 marks]** (e) The sum of the roots of the equation is equal to twice their product. Find the possible values of \(k\). **[4 marks]**
Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be the roots of the quadratic equation $2x^2 - 4x - 3 = 0$. Find the quadratic equation whose roots are $\alpha^2$ and $\beta^2$.

A quadratic equation is given by $$ (k-1)x^2 + 2(k+1)x + (2k-3) = 0, $$ where \(k\) is a real parameter. (a) Find the values of \(k\) for which the equation has equal roots. [4 marks] (b) Determine the range of values of \(k\) for which the equation has two distinct real roots. [4 marks] (c) Find the value(s) of \(k\) for which the equation has no real roots. [3 marks] (d) For \(k=2\), solve the resulting quadratic equation by completing the square. [4 marks] (e) A rectangular garden has length \(3\,\text{m}\) more than twice its width. The area of the garden is \(90\,\text{m}^2\). Form a quadratic equation in the width and solve it to find the dimensions of the garden. [5 marks]
Find the middle term in the binomial expansion of \(\left(3 - \frac{x}{3}\right)^{10}\).

Use the binomial theorem to expand $(1+4x)^{\frac{1}{2}}$ in ascending powers of $x$ up to and including the term in $x^3$. Hence, by substituting $x=\frac{1}{48}$, obtain an approximation to $\sqrt{3}$ correct to 3 decimal places.

(a) Write down the first four terms in ascending powers of $x$ in the expansion of $(1+x)^{1/2}$. By taking $x=0.02$, obtain $\sqrt{1.02}$ correct to 4 decimal places. [8 marks] (b) Use the first three terms of a binomial expansion to find an approximate value of $\sqrt{0.99}$ correct to 3 decimal places. [4 marks] (c) From a group of 6 men and 7 women, how many different committees consisting of 3 men and 5 women can be formed if Jane, Joyce and John must always be together? [5 marks] (d) Find the number of distinguishable arrangements of the letters of the word DISSAPPOINTMENTS. [3 marks]

A student is revising the binomial theorem and its applications. (a) Solve the quadratic equation $x^2 - 4x + 8 = 0$. (b) A gallery owner has 9 distinct paintings and wall space to display only 4 of them at a time. In how many different ways can the owner choose and arrange 4 paintings on the wall? (c) Find the coefficient of $x^3$ in the expansion of $(1 - 3x)^{15}$. (d) A class contains 12 boys and 16 girls. In how many ways can a committee of 4 people be formed if there must be at least 2 girls on the committee? (e) Use the binomial theorem to expand $(8 - 3x)^{1/3}$ in ascending powers of $x$ up to and including the term in $x^2$. Hence, by taking a suitable value of $x$, obtain an approximation for $\sqrt[3]{7.7}$ correct to 4 decimal places.
Find the constant term in the expansion of \(\left(2x - \dfrac{3}{x^2}\right)^{12}\).

These medals were awarded to a total of 45 persons, and exactly 4 persons received medals in all three categories. Determine how many persons received medals in exactly two of the categories.
